body.p: If indicated, please amend the claims accordingly.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) An air-permeable bedding system, comprising:
an inlet configured to be connected to an active air source;
a microclimate fabric layer; and
an air-permeable capacitive sensor layer below the microclimate fabric layer, the air- permeable capacitive sensor layer comprises comprising a top air-permeable substrate, [[and]] a bottom air-permeable substrate, and an air-permeable dielectric layer, wherein:the top and bottom air-permeable substrates are separated vertically by the air- permeable dielectric layer that is located between the top and bottom air- permeable substrates,
the air-permeable dielectric layer is configured to receive air flow horizontally from the active air source,
the air-permeable dielectric layer comprises a plurality of cut-outs,
wherein the top air-permeable substrate is laminated with carries a top set of electrically conductive pathways, [[and]] the bottom air-permeable substrate is laminated with carries a bottom set of electronically electrically conductive pathways,
the electrically conductive pathways of the top set of electrically conductive pathways are parallel to each other and the electrically conductive pathways of the bottom set of electrically conductive pathways are parallelApplication No.: 17/019,090 to each other and the top set and the bottom set are rotated being arranged at an angle [[of]] relative to each other to form a grid,
the parallel electrically conductive pathways in the top set are being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a top set of horizontal air pathways= [[and]] the parallel electrically conductive pathways in the bottom set are being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a bottom set of horizontal air pathways,
the top and bottom sets of electrically conductive pathways separated vertically by [[an]] the air-permeable dielectric layer that is configured to receive air flow horizontally from the active air source is located between the top and bottom air-permeable substrates, wherein the top and bottom sets of horizontal air pathways intersect with each other and intersect with the cut-outs of the air-permeable dielectric layer to form air- permeable substrates respectively position the top and bottom sets of electrically conductive pathways to cross over each other forming a grid, forming capacitors at intersection points of the grid, and forming vertical air-pathways at a plurality of gaps of the grid, and wherein the dielectric layer and the top and bottom air-permeable substrates comprise cut-outs at the vertical air pathways such that airflow passes vertically through the plurality of gaps of the grid and horizontally through the air-permeable dielectric layer[[.]], andApplication No.: 17/019,090 one of the top set and the bottom set of electrically conductive pathways is configured to transmit electrical signals and another one of the top set and the bottom set of electrically conductive pathways is configured to receive the electrical signals.
2. (Canceled)
3. (Previously Presented) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein the top air-permeable substrate and bottom air-permeable substrate are formed from meshes or foam.
4. (Currently Amended) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein at least one electrically conductive pathway of the top and bottom sets of electrically conductive pathways carried by one of the top and bottom air-permeable substrates is encapsulated by a thermoplastic.
5. (Previously Presented) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 4, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the one of the top and bottom air-permeable substrates.
6. (Previously Presented) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 5, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the one of the top and bottom air-permeable substrates by heat lamination.
7. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a foam comfort layer between the microclimate fabric layer and the air-permeable capacitive sensor layer.
8. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a piezoelectric sensor below the microclimate fabric layer.
9. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 8, further comprising a transmitter configured to transmit signals of the capacitive sensor layer for determining a respiration rate and to transmit signals of the piezoelectric sensor for determining a heart rate.
10. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
an inlet configured to be connected to an active air source that increases airflow within the air-permeable bedding system.
11. (Withdrawn) A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, a target body part of a person on the bedding system;
identifying a subset of the pressure sensor data generated from a region of the sensor grid that measures pressure exerted by the target body part; and
using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine a heart rate or a respiration rate of the person.
12. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, the target body part of the person on the bedding system comprises:
identifying the person's body and joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data, and
identifying the target body part based on the joint positions.Application No.: 17/019,090
13. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 12, wherein identifying the person's body and target joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure data, and
inputting the matrix of pressure data to a machine learning model for identifying the target joint positions.
14. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine the heart rate or the respiration rate of the person comprises:
calculating an average pressure corresponding to the region based on the subset of the pressure sensor data,
generating a time series of pressure readings corresponding to the region, and
determining the heart rate or the respiration rate based on the time series.
15. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein the target body part is a lumbar area of the person.
16. (Withdrawn) A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving a time series of pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying poses of a person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data;
determining respiration rates of the person based on the pressure sensor data; and
inputting the poses and the respiration rates of the person to a machine learning model to determine a sleep state of the person.Application No.: 17/019,090
17. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein identifying the poses of the person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging, for a particular instance in time, the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure readings,
inputting the matrix of pressure readings to a machine learning model for a particular pose at the particular instance, and
generating other poses in other instances in time using the machine learning model.
18. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the poses and the respiration rates are formatted as two additional time series.
19. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the sleep state is one of candidate sleep states, and the machine learning model generates a probability that the person is in a particular candidate sleep state for each candidate state, the sleep state selected being the particular candidate sleep state with the highest probability.
20. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, further comprising:
determining heart rates of the person, wherein the machine learning model also receives the heart rates to determine the sleep state of the person.
